title.provenance: Section 1. This Act may be referred to as the PFAS Consumer Protection Law.

pfas_definition.provenance: "PFAS chemical" means any of the perfluoroalkyl substances or polyfluoroalkyl substances included in the United States Environmental Protection Agency's expanded ToxCast chemical inventory.

products.provenance: (c) On and after January 1, 2025, no person shall sell, offer for sale, distribute for sale, or distribute for use in the State any product in any of the following product categories if the product contains an intentionally added PFAS chemical: ... (1) Carpets or rugs. (2) Fabric treatments. (3) Food packaging. (4) Juvenile products. (5) Oil and gas products. (6) Apparel.

value: Products sold or resold before the effective date of this amendatory Act of the 103rd General Assembly

Internal component of what would otherwise constitute a juvenile product but that would not come into direct contact with a child's skin or mouth during the reasonably foreseeable use or abuse of the juvenile product by a child
exceptions.provenance: "Product" does not include any of the following: (1) A drug, medical device, biologic, or diagnostic approved or authorized by the United States Food and Drug Administration or the United States Department of Agriculture. (2) Veterinary pesticide products approved by the United States Environmental Protection Agency for use in animals. (3) A material used in the packaging of the materials described in paragraphs (1) and (2). (4) A product sold or resold before the effective date of this amendatory Act of the 103rd General Assembly.

intentionally_added.provenance: "Intentionally added PFAS chemical" means a PFAS chemical that a PFAS manufacturer has intentionally added to a product and that has a functional or technical effect on the product.

type.provenance: (f) On and after January 1, 2025, a PFAS manufacturer of cookware sold in this State that contains an intentionally added PFAS chemical in the handle of the cookware or in any surface of the cookware that comes into contact with food, foodstuffs, or beverages shall list the presence of PFAS chemicals on the cookware's product label.

value: Cookware that does not have any of the following: (A) An exterior container or wrapper upon which a product label can appear or be affixed. (B) A tag or label to which information about the cookware may be attached.
exceptions.provenance: (h) Cookware is exempt from this Section if it meets all of the following requirements: (1) The surface area of the cookware is not large enough for a product label that meets the requirements of subsection (f) to be affixed to the item. (2) The cookware does not have any of the following: (A) An exterior container or wrapper upon which a product label can appear or be affixed. (B) A tag or label to which information about the cookware may be attached.
